# Right-size the llama-server prompt cache and checkpoint budget

**Headline:** The 40 GiB prompt cache saturates again — 39,829 of 40,960 MiB with
26 prompts on 2026-11-03, and 38.5 GiB resident right now — so this item
measures how much re-prefill is caused by eviction rather than by genuinely new
tokens, and right-sizes the two knobs that set per-prompt cost (`cache-ram` and
`ctx-checkpoints`) from that measurement rather than from the 16-prompt estimate
the current cap was derived from.

## Problem statement

When the prompt cache reaches its cap, llama-server evicts the oldest cached
prompt and that session's next turn becomes a full prefill of its whole context
(tens of thousands of tokens, up to several hundred seconds) instead of a short
delta prefill. The cache is currently sized from a per-prompt state estimate of
~2,013 MiB measured against a maximum of 16 concurrently-retained prompts; the
2026-11-03 incident shows 26 prompts with the cache at 97.2% of its cap and
592,452 prompt tokens consumed for 4,345 decoded tokens in 40 minutes. The
estimate and the real load have diverged, and nothing records whether the
resulting re-prefill is eviction waste or genuinely new work.

## Users

- **Proxy operator (agent, on-call, or the next maintainer)** — needs a cache
  budget that stops silently evicting under normal load, plus a recorded
  derivation and host-memory floor so the number is not re-litigated from a new
  round number.
- **Agent sessions on the local model** (pi sessions, herdr workers, remote LAN
  clients) — pay the re-prefill as minutes of first-byte latency on a turn they
  have effectively already sent.
- **Maintainers of the tuning docs and tests** — need the documented geometry,
  the pinning test and the configured values to agree, so drift is a red test
  rather than a future incident.

User stories:

- As an agent session returning to the local model after a pause, I want my
  prefix still resident so my next turn is a delta prefill, not a full one.
- As a proxy operator, I want the cache budget derived from a measured
  per-prompt size and a stated headroom floor, so a busy week cannot push the
  host into swap.
- As a maintainer, I want the cache numbers in `models.ini`, the tuning doc and
  the pinning test to agree, and the re-prefill attribution measured rather than
  assumed.

## Evidence

Recorded incident (2026-11-03, 08:30–09:10), from
`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` and `llama-server.log`:

| observation | value |
|---|---|
| prompt cache in use | 39,829 MiB of the 40,960 MiB cap |
| prompts retained | 26, several holding the full 32 checkpoints (2,925 / 2,998 / 2,494 MiB each) |
| cache update latency | 234 ms |
| slot `prompt_save` state written per task switch | 439 MiB |
| prompt tokens processed / decoded | 592,452 / 4,345 (≈136:1) |
| prefill rates in the log | median 122 tok/s; 143–303 tok/s for the large re-prefills; 598 tok/s best case |

Current live state (2026-11-18): host total 127,436 MiB, `MemAvailable`
46,907 MiB, 1,042 MiB of swap in use; the spawned Qwen3 child carries
`--cache-ram 40960`, `--swa-checkpoints 32`, `--parallel 2` and has been resident
since 2026-11-15 with RSS grown to 38.5 GiB — i.e. the cap is filling again
under normal load, three days after the last restart.

Prior measurements at the same cap, for contrast:

| window | cap | requests | evictions | max prompts held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-12 (`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`) | 32,768 MiB | 1,404 | 18 | 16 |
| 2026-10-18 (`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18.json`) | 40,960 MiB | 380 | 0 | 11 |
| 2026-11-03 incident | 40,960 MiB | — | — | 26 |

The 2026-10-18 window recorded zero evictions, so the cap looked adequate then;
the growth to 26 retained prompts is a load change, not a regression in the
sizing arithmetic. That is precisely why the per-prompt constant must be
re-derived against the current prompt count instead of the 16-prompt figure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Attribution is measured, not assumed** — over a fixed, named window a reproducible measurement (committed script or artifact) decomposes prefilled prompt tokens into (a) genuinely new tokens, where the prompt or prefix was never cached (new session or genuine divergence), and (b) re-prefills of a prefix that was previously cached and then lost, reporting the eviction-attributable share and token volume; the attribution method, its match rule and its error bounds or limitations are stated alongside the numbers.
2. **A trade-off table supports the recommendation** — the measurement produces a `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table stating, per candidate configuration: prompts held, per-prompt state, the checkpoint term, killed prompts (prompts that would no longer fit), the checkpoint resume value (rollback granularity and the full-prefill risk of having fewer anchors), and MiB per prompt; the recommended pair is derived from that table and names the `MemAvailable` floor at which an increase must be refused.
3. **Applied, durable and pinned by test** — the chosen values are applied in `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with a comment recording the measurement, its date and the derivation; the expectations in `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` now assert the chosen values, and `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` states the same derivation so config, doc and test cannot drift apart.
4. **Post-change verification, deployed** — the change is deployed with `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never by killing the proxy) and the spawned Qwen3 child is confirmed to carry the new flags; a post-change measurement over a window comparable to the AC1 baseline shows both the eviction-attributable re-prefill share and prefilled prompt tokens per request falling measurably, with the prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio recorded alongside its workload caveat.
5. **No throughput or latency regression** — prompt-eval throughput and client-visible first-byte latency measured over the same before/after windows do not regress, or any movement is attributed with evidence to a named confounder rather than to this change.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Local sessions stop losing their cached prefixes to eviction, so a returning session's first token arrives in seconds of delta prefill instead of minutes of full re-prefill.

## Constraints

- **Config must be durable**: values are set through `models.ini` `[Qwen3]`, not
  a one-off launch-script switch, so they survive a proxy restart (the precedent
  set by LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L AC7).
- **Host memory is shared**: 128 GiB unified memory, of which the model weights
  (24.6 GiB, `Q5_K_M`), the q8_0 KV cache and the prompt cache all draw from the
  same pool that the GPU uses. The documented invariant is
  `MemAvailable - cache-ram >= max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)` = 12,743.7 MiB.
- **The pinning test is a hard gate**: `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh`
  asserts `cache-ram = 40960` and `ctx-checkpoints = 32`; any change to either
  knob must update those assertions in the same commit.
- **llama-server logs carry no timestamps**: a measurement window is a *file
  set*, so the corpus (and its file list) must be recorded in the artifact's
  `meta` block for the before/after comparison to be reproducible.
- **Expected-but-not-an-error log line**: `forcing full prompt re-processing due
  to lack of cache data` is normal for this hybrid attention + recurrent
  architecture; the signal is its *volume* and the token count behind it, never
  the message itself.
- **Test execution routes through `/skill:test`**; no ad-hoc `pytest` runs.
- **Never kill the LLM proxy** — use `/skill:start-proxy --restart` for the
  deploy step.

## Existing state

- `models.ini` `[Qwen3]`: `cache-ram = 40960` (derived 2026-10-12 from
  2,013 MiB/prompt x 16 observed max x 1.25), `ctx-checkpoints = 32` (pinned at
  the llama.cpp default, with a comment explaining why it is not the lever),
  `swa-full` removed as a no-op for this arch.
- `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` already measures requests, prompt tokens
  requested/reused/prefilled, full prefills split small/large, prefill wall time,
  eviction count and sizes, cache saturation and checkpoint overhead, and
  supports `--recommend`, `--json`, `--glob`, `--cache-ram-filter` and
  `--assume-cache-ram-mib`. It does **not** yet attribute a full prefill to an
  eviction, and `recommend()` proposes a `cache-ram` only — it reports the
  checkpoint term but does not vary it.
- Committed measurement artifacts: `docs/dev/prompt-cache-baseline-2026-10-01.json`,
  `-post-deploy-2026-10-07/10-12/10-15-partial/10-18*.json`.
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` documents the sizing history, the checkpoint
  lever's "kept at 32" decision and the headroom invariant.
- The 2026-11-03 saturation is not yet measured with the tool: there is no
  artifact for that window, and no figure for how much of the 592,452 prompt
  tokens was eviction-caused.

## Desired change

Extend the measurement so a full prefill is attributed to an eviction rather
than to genuinely new work, then use that attribution to choose the
`cache-ram` / `ctx-checkpoints` pair, record the derivation in `models.ini` and
the tuning doc, pin it in the test, deploy, and verify the improvement on a
comparable window. The outcome is explicitly allowed to be "the current sizing
is correct and the residual re-prefill is genuinely new tokens" — provided the
measurement and the decision are recorded.

Three live items converge on one `models.ini` comment block and one
`ctx-checkpoints` value (`LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV`, `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51`, this
item). Sequencing, not silent merging, is the mitigation — see the scope
boundaries and risks.

## Scope boundary and non-goals

- **Not** slot count or slot geometry (`LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` territory; slot
  geometry was separately measured at 0 tok/s in
  `docs/dev/local-prefill-lever-comparison-2026-11-11.md`).
- **Not** KV-cache quantisation (`cache-type-k/v`) or weight quantisation.
- **Not** `force_full_prompt` / delta routing — that flag is load-bearing for
  this hybrid arch (LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L investigation) and removing it would
  break context, not improve caching.
- **Not** `ubatch-size` — measured and reverted (1.04x at ~27k tokens, below the
  1.3x gate); do not re-raise without a 40–80k-token measurement.
- **Not** the proxy's own disk slot save/restore path (`session_slot_*`), which
  is bypassed and worthless for a hybrid/recurrent model (llama.cpp#25913).
- **Scope boundary with `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV`** ("Re-derive cache-ram with a
  MemAvailable floor", a blocked child of epic `LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS`): that item
  owns the geometry sync test and the durable floor wording. This item's AC3
  writes the same comment block, so the two must not be implemented in parallel.
  If this item lands first it satisfies that slice's "measurement refresh", and
  the producer can close `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` as already covered rather than
  paying for a second derivation.
- **Scope boundary with `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51`** ("Launch-flag A/B: threads and
  SWA checkpoints", blocked): that item has `--swa-checkpoints` (the
  `--ctx-checkpoints` alias) explicitly **in scope** as a benchmark A/B, and its
  own AC1 predicts the signal will be a change in the
  `forcing full prompt re-processing` path rather than raw throughput — i.e. the
  same question this item asks from production logs. The split is by method and
  evidence, not by knob: this item **consumes** any value that item has already
  measured and adopted (it becomes the candidate configuration), and **does not
  re-litigate** an adopted value silently — a conflict between the A/B result
  and this item's attribution measurement is recorded and escalated, not
  resolved by picking the friendlier number. Three items touching one knob is
  itself a sequencing risk worth flagging to the producer.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Attribution has no explicit join key.** The llama-server log does not tag a
  prefill with the cache entry it would have matched, so attribution must be
  inferred (for example: a full prefill whose token count matches a recently
  evicted entry within a bounded window, cross-checked against the proxy's
  per-dispatch `cached_ratio`). AC1 therefore requires the match rule *and* its
  error bounds to be stated, and a deliberately conservative classification is
  preferred over an optimistic one.
- **Raising `cache-ram` is not free.** The host is already at 46.9 GiB
  `MemAvailable` with swap in use; an increase sized against 26 prompts
  (~49 GiB by the current arithmetic) is unlikely to clear the floor. The
  checkpoint lever (halving `ctx-checkpoints` halves the ~2 GiB per-prompt term)
  is the likely answer, and it buys capacity at the cost of coarser rollback.
- **The headroom invariant double-counts a resident cache.** The documented
  check is `MemAvailable - cache-ram >= reserve`, which is a pre-allocation test;
  when the cache is already fully resident, only the *delta* is a real
  allocation. Whichever form is used must be stated in the recorded derivation,
  because the two give different verdicts today.
- **Fewer checkpoints can increase full prefills.** Fewer anchors means less
  chance of matching a reused prefix. If the checkpoint lever is taken, AC4's
  post-change measurement is what proves it helped rather than hurt, and the
  prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio must not be the only evidence — it is
  workload-dependent and a quieter week would flatter it. Per-request metrics
  (`prefilled tokens/request`, `eviction-attributable prefills/request`) are the
  comparable ones.
- **Scope-creep risk**: the measurement will surface adjacent findings (cache
  update latency, `prompt_save` write volume, admission behaviour). These are
  recorded as observation bullets or as `discovered-from` work items, not
  absorbed into this item's ACs.
- **Assumption**: the 2026-11-03 window's logs are still available under
  `/var/log/llama-proxy/` (rotated or not) for the baseline; if they have
  rotated away, the baseline is the nearest surviving window and that
  substitution is recorded in the artifact with the corpus file list.

**Key Files:**

- `models.ini` — `[Qwen3]` `cache-ram` / `ctx-checkpoints` and the derivation comment block (AC2, AC3)
- `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` — needs an eviction-attribution split in the summary (AC1) and a checkpoint term in `recommend()` (AC2)
- `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py` — attribution and recommendation cases (AC1, AC2)
- `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` — the two pinned assertions (`cache-ram = 40960` ~line 560, `ctx-checkpoints = 32` ~line 573) (AC3)
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` — checkpoint-lever section, headroom invariant and the new measurement (AC3, AC6)
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-<window>.json` — the committed before/after measurement artifacts (AC1, AC4)
- `proxy/proxy/` — read-only unless the proxy's per-dispatch `cached_ratio` is needed for the attribution cross-check (AC1)

## Related work

- **LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L** (completed) — the original prompt-cache right-sizing
  (8 GiB default -> 23,552 MiB), which built `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`
  and `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` and first documented the checkpoint
  term as the dominant per-prompt cost.
- **LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN** and **LP-0MV5HSUHF002MDPG** (completed) — the
  32,768 MiB and 40,960 MiB cap raises, and the 2,013 MiB/prompt x 16 x 1.25
  derivation this item re-derives against 26 prompts.
- **LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW** (completed) — the post-deploy verification pattern
  (baseline artifact, length-matched window, before/after table) that AC1 and
  AC4 should follow.
- **LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS** (epic, plan_complete) — "Keep local prompt prefixes
  resident", whose AC3 is the cache-headroom commitment this item feeds; its
  child **LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV** is the overlapping derivation slice (scope
  boundary above) and **LP-0MW3GKXQS004F3CC** is the geometry sync test.
- **LP-0MVKU2J0T0023RRW** (blocked) — characterising restored-cache
  invalidation on this hybrid arch; relevant because it constrains what a
  checkpoint change can be expected to buy.
- **LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51** (blocked) — the launch-flag A/B on threads and SWA
  checkpoints. It has `--swa-checkpoints` in scope with the same re-prefill
  hypothesis, so its result is an input to AC2 rather than a separate answer
  (scope boundary above).
- **LP-0MWCEII0V003V76A / `docs/dev/local-prefill-lever-comparison-2026-11-11.md`**
  — the four-family prefill lever register (slot geometry 0 tok/s, quant at most
  1.9%, parallel prefill 1.00x), which is why cache capacity, not batch or
  geometry, is the lever left to pull here.

## Related work (automated report)

- **LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV** – Re-derive cache-ram with a MemAvailable floor (blocked)
- **LP-0MW3GKXQS004F3CC** – Cache geometry sync test (open)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**No producer questions were required for this intake.** The seed context
(2026-11-03 incident evidence plus three testable ACs) and the producer's
2026-11-05 answers on the parent epic resolved every open decision:

- Q: *May `cache-ram` be raised above 40,960 MiB, or must the fallback (reduce
  the checkpoint set / cap concurrent prompts) be the planned remediation?* —
  Answer (producer, 2026-11-05, recorded on `LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS`): "Host RAM:
  128 GiB unified memory — cache-ram increase permitted subject to a stated
  MemAvailable floor." Source: `wl show LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS` comment by Map,
  2026-11-05T11:14:47Z. Consequence: no producer gate on the cache-ram lever;
  the floor decides, which is why AC2 requires the floor to be named.
- Q: *Is reducing `ctx-checkpoints` acceptable given the documented "fewer
  checkpoints can increase full prefills" conclusion?* — Answer (research):
  acceptable only as the fallback, since AC2's original wording asks for "the
  measured trade-off stated" and AC3 explicitly permits a recorded no-change
  decision. Evidence: `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` comment block and
  `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` §"Checkpoint lever (AC3)". No question
  raised because the item already admits both outcomes.
- Q: *Does this item duplicate the epic's `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` ("Re-derive
  cache-ram with a MemAvailable floor")?* — Answer (research, duplicate-check
  procedure): partial overlap only. That item re-derives `cache-ram` and adds
  the MemAvailable floor plus a doc/test sync; it explicitly does not touch
  `ctx-checkpoints`, does not attribute re-prefill to eviction, and does not
  measure a post-change window. This item keeps those distinctive parts (AC1,
  AC2's checkpoint half, AC4) and records the shared-comment-block conflict as
  a scope boundary rather than rewriting the other item.

**Research summary.** The 8 GiB -> 23,552 -> 32,768 -> 40,960 MiB history, the
2,013 MiB/prompt derivation and the "checkpoint term is ~2 GiB of the ~2 GiB"
finding all come from `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` and the
`docs/dev/prompt-cache-*.json` artifacts. The live confirmation (40,960 MiB
resident, RSS 38.5 GiB after 3.3 days, `MemAvailable` 46,907 MiB with swap in
use) was read from `ps`/`free` on 2026-11-18. The hard-pinned test assertions
were found at `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh:560-582`. The three
"prior measurement" rows were recomputed from the committed JSON artifacts.

## Plan (decomposition)

Decomposed into five child slices, created test-first and wired as a serial dependency chain (each slice is a vertical cut through code, tests, docs and — from slice 2 — a committed measurement artifact):

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction-attribution fixtures and red tests (LP-0MWLZPTY1001QR4T) | task | — | AC1, AC2 (executable contract) |
| 2 | Attribute full prefills to evictions (LP-0MWLZPUKD000D2NG) | feature | 1 | AC1 |
| 3 | cache-ram x ctx-checkpoints trade-off table (LP-0MWLZPV7A005JZJD) | feature | 2 | AC2 |
| 4 | Apply and pin the chosen geometry (LP-0MWLZPVUG004ECFL) | feature | 3 | AC3, AC6 (code comments/doc) |
| 5 | Deploy and verify the post-change window (LP-0MWLZPWHO006NVVF) | task | 4 | AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7 |

Ordering rationale: the parent's outcome is explicitly allowed to be "the current sizing is correct", so the measurement (slice 2) and its table (slice 3) must produce evidence before any knob is touched (slice 4); the deploy and verification (slice 5) is a separate slice because it is the only one that interrupts service and because its evidence window is bounded by the restart.

Deploy sequencing recorded as an implementation note, not a plan dependency: `/skill:start-proxy --restart` kills llama-server, so any request in flight fails and the prompt cache restarts empty. The restart is detached and health-polled by the start-proxy skill, so it runs safely between tool calls; the post-change window starts at the restart timestamp.

Scope boundaries carried into the children (not merged silently): `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` (blocked) owns a slice of the same `models.ini` comment block and floor wording — slice 4 comments there recording that this item wrote the shared block; `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51` (blocked) owns the `--swa-checkpoints` A/B — slice 3 consumes any value it has already adopted and escalates a conflict rather than picking the friendlier number.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18: decomposed into 5 child slices (1 test, 3 feature, 1 verification) with a serial dependency chain; effort/risk re-estimated; plan Appendix recorded. No child closed, rewritten or duplicated (duplicate check found no fully-covered existing item; `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` is partial overlap and stays as a blocked sibling under the scope boundary above).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session)

**No blocking producer questions.** The intake Appendix already records the producer's 2026-11-05 answers (cache-ram increase permitted subject to a stated `MemAvailable` floor; the checkpoint lever acceptable as the fallback), so the plan was resolved from repository evidence. Four research questions were answered from the tree and are recorded here for auditability.

- Q: *Does the 2026-11-03 incident window survive on disk for the AC1 baseline?* — Answer (research): No. `/var/log/llama-proxy/` retains daily rotation files from `llama-server.log-2026-11-04.gz` (922 B, effectively empty) onward; real content starts 2026-11-07. Consequence: the baseline is the nearest surviving saturated window, with the substitution and corpus file list in the artifact `meta` — the fallback the item's own risks section already allows. Evidence: `ls -l /var/log/llama-proxy/`, 2026-11-18.
- Q: *Which surviving window is the best baseline substitute?* — Answer (research): the surviving corpora are **busier** than the incident, so the substitution strengthens rather than weakens the evidence. Cache-state maxima measured 2026-11-18: 26 prompts (2026-11-07), 27 (11-08), 24 (11-09), 29 (11-10), 31 (11-11 and `llama-server.2.log`, 14 MB), 11 (11-12), 47 (11-13). Candidate baseline named in slice 2: 2026-11-13 (largest prompt count).
- Q: *Which `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` candidates belong in the AC2 table?* — Answer (research): `ctx-checkpoints` in {32, 16, 8} x `cache-ram` in {current 40,960 MiB, the measured requirement at the observed prompt maximum, the same capacity reached with a halved checkpoint term}, plus any value already adopted by `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51`. Rationale: the checkpoint term is ~2 GiB of the ~2 GiB per-prompt cost, so halving checkpoints halves per-prompt state; the item's risks section names this as the likely answer while requiring the reported resume-value cost. No producer decision needed — both levers are already authorised by the intake Appendix.

## Goal

**As an** operator reading the after-acceptance eviction signal, **I want** a local dispatch that **completed successfully** to be released without being reported as `local_eviction_after_acceptance`, **so that** the AC7(a) defect detector (LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S) counts real evictions instead of ordinary lease expiry.

## Evidence (2026-11-03 14:25:54 → 14:26:34 UTC, `dev` `7892d22d`)

A small verification request that **succeeded in 0.57 s** was 40 s later reported as an eviction after acceptance:

```
14:25:54  routing_check provider=local-qwen3 ... estimated_tokens=8
14:25:54  [local] POST ...  Stream finished: reason=length tokens=18/8/26 stream=false
14:25:54  lease_renewed session=verify-... timeout=30s
14:25:54  local_preference_resolved preference=remote-ok outcome=local reason=none
14:26:34  local_eviction     ... reason=slot_assignment_freed slot=0
14:26:34  local_eviction_after_acceptance ... reason=idle_timeout estimated_tokens=8
          new_tokens=8 eta_prefill_s=0.0 elapsed_s=40.1
14:26:34  lease_released session=verify-... reason=idle_timeout
```

Three things are wrong together:

1. `local_eviction_after_acceptance` is documented as "accepted local dispatches evicted **before their first byte**" — this request produced its first byte (and its last) within 0.57 s, so it was never evicted *after acceptance* in the intended sense;
2. `elapsed_s=40.1` is the *lease's* idle lifetime (30 s timeout + slack), not the request duration — so the field mixes two different clocks;
3. the event is emitted on the routine `lease_released ... reason=idle_timeout` path, which is the normal way every completed local dispatch's record expires.

Measured frequency in this window: 7 `local_eviction` lines, 6 `reason=slot_assignment_freed` (expected churn) and 1 `reason=idle_timeout` — i.e. 100 % of the `idle_timeout` eviction reports in the sample are false positives, and the true-positive rate of the signal cannot be established while that is the case.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event is emitted only when a dispatch was admitted and did **not** reach its first byte (the documented meaning); a completed or cancelled-after-first-byte dispatch releases silently or under its own reason.
- AC2: `elapsed_s` measures the request's own lifetime (admission → release), not the lease timeout, so the value agrees with the request's observed duration.
- AC3: A regression test drives the pattern above — one local dispatch that completes, then the idle lease release — and asserts **no** `local_eviction_after_acceptance` line; a second test drives a genuine admitted-then-never-first-byte dispatch and asserts the line **is** emitted with a truthful `elapsed_s`.
- AC4: Existing consumers keep working: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` stays a distinct event from `local_eviction`, its `reason` vocabulary is unchanged, and the usage-analysis report's after-acceptance breakdown (which splits by reason) still renders.
- AC5: Documentation of the event's meaning in `proxy/docs/routing.md` matches the behaviour.

## Out of scope

- The eviction reasons themselves (`measured_cache_deficit`, `prefill_deadline`, `idle_timeout`) and their thresholds.
- Any change to how leases are released — only to what is *reported* about the release.

## Key files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` — the `local_eviction` / `local_eviction_after_acceptance` emitters.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the idle-timeout / slot-assignment-free release paths and the dispatcher that records the event.
- `proxy/tests/` — `test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`, `test_lease_truthfulness.py`, and the usage-analysis `test_post_acceptance_eviction_report.py` contract.

## Assumptions

- The `slot_assignment_freed` line emitted immediately before it is the expected churn line and is not part of the defect.
- The window's single occurrence is representative of the routine path (every completed local dispatch leaves a record that later expires by `idle_timeout`), not a one-off; AC1/AC3 make that checkable rather than assumed.

# Orphaned `local_prefill_in_flight` marker closes the local route for every session (429 "Local admission refused")

## Impact

Operators can trust the local route to stay open: an orphaned in-flight-prefill marker can no longer deny every locally-pinned request with `429 Local admission refused` while the GPU is idle and llama-server reports free slots.

## Problem statement

Since **2026-11-17 14:24:42** the running proxy denied *every* local dispatch because one orphaned in-flight-prefill marker is counted by the dispatch gate:

```
local_dispatch_denied ... owner=none active=1 records_total=0 records_active=0
  records_unexpired=0 records_stale=0 active_counter=0 max_local=2 generating=0
  prefill_in_flight=1 prefill_cap=1 llama_available_slots=2 llama_total_slots=2
```

Zero dispatch records, nothing generating, llama-server reporting 2 free slots — yet `prefill_in_flight=1` against `prefill_cap=1` (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`). The status endpoint disagreed on the same machine at the same moment:

```
GET /llama/local/status
local_prefills_in_flight=0  available_slots=2  capacity_hint=idle
local_in_flight_requests=0  local_route_available=true
```

Consequences observed in `/tmp/proxy-startup-20261116T152048Z-3719311.log`:

- 505 `local_dispatch_denied ... records_total=0` lines since 14:24:42 (all 1225 denial lines in the log carry `prefill_in_flight=1`).
- 413 `local_only_refused ... preference=local-preferred verdict=deferrable` refusals, split `cause=queue_depth_exceeded` (160) / `cause=queue_wait_expired` (187) after the 30 s contention-queue wait.
- Every herdr-dispatched pane (`X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`) died with `429 {"error": "Local admission refused", "code": "local_admission_reject"}` because a *deferrable* pin is contractually never promoted to a paid provider (`LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY`). Sessions sending `remote-ok` still worked — they fell through to `opencode-go-3`, which masked the wedge.

## Users

- **Operators of the local GPU pool** — need the local route to reopen by itself after a dispatch dies without a clean release; today a single orphan needs either a proxy restart or a hand-issued `POST /v1/leases/release`.
- **herdr-dispatched agents (local-only pins)** — their session is pinned with `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, so a wedged gate is a hard outage for them, not a fallback.

Stories:

- *As an operator*, when a lease dies without a clean release, I want the admission gate to stop counting it, so the local pool serves the next session instead of refusing everything until I notice.
- *As a local-pinned agent session*, I want a peer session's orphaned marker to be invisible to my admission decision, so I am admitted whenever a slot is genuinely free.

## Root cause (two defects, one symptom)

1. **Gate counts orphaned markers.** `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:4712` (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) prices the prefill cap with `_get_prefill_in_flight_count()`, which is `len(srv.local_prefill_in_flight)` — raw, including markers with no live dispatch record. The liveness-filtered `_get_live_prefill_in_flight_count()` (`router_helpers.py:3762`, added by `LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O` AC3) already implements the correct accounting and is used by the status payload and admission pricing, but **not** by the dispatch gate. With `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` a single orphan closes the local route permanently.
2. **Record pruning leaks the marker.** `_prune_stale_dispatch_records()` (`router_helpers.py:7960`, marker deletion at `router_helpers.py:7990`) deletes an inactive record past `expires_at` and frees its slot assignment, but never pops the session's `local_prefill_in_flight` entry. The explicit-release, client-disconnect, request-completion, watchdog and orphan-sweep paths all pop it; this one does not.

Verified at HEAD `9a8c75208`: the gate call site still uses the raw helper, and `proxy/proxy/session.py` contains **no** reference to `local_prefill_in_flight`, so `_invalidate_session_and_slot` (`session.py:1722`) — which pops the dispatch records — also leaves the marker behind. That is the second deletion path lacking the pop, and it is what AC4 must close.

## Measured sequence (incident timeline)

- `01a1e9e4-90be-70d7-a899-aa39b5c753ca` held the only dispatch: `lease_renewed` at 14:23:54 / 14:23:57 / 14:24:02 / 14:24:10, no `lease_released` ever logged for it.
- 14:24:12–14:24:34: other sessions denied with `owner=01a1e9e4-90be-…`, `records_total=1 records_active=0` (inactive lease retention).
- 14:24:42: `_prune_stale_dispatch_records` removed that record → `records_total=0, owner=none`, but `prefill_in_flight=1` remained.
- 14:24:42 → mitigation: every local dispatch denied; local route idle since 14:24 (`local_idle_seconds=6533` at 16:10) while refusals continued.

## Existing state

- **Immediate mitigation (no restart) — applied and verified.** The marker is process memory (`proxy/proxy/server.py:134`), so a restart clears it; a targeted `POST /v1/leases/release {"session_id": "<leaked session>"}` is sufficient while the proxy must keep running, because `_release_local_dispatch` pops `local_prefill_in_flight[session_id]` unconditionally, even when no record exists (idempotent). Applied to this incident's leaked session `01a1e9e4-90be-70d7-a899-aa39b5c753ca`; denial lines went from a ~7 s cadence (505 in total) to **0** for the following 2+ minutes, and local serving resumed (`local_preference_resolved ... outcome=local` → `Stream started: provider=local`).
- The mitigation is per-orphan and manual: the defect recurs on the next prune of a record whose marker was never popped, so the code fix is still required.
- Existing seams to build on: `_get_live_prefill_in_flight_count` (live-filtered count), `_prune_stale_dispatch_records` (named so the invariant has a unit-test seam, already exercised by `proxy/tests/test_local_lease_occupancy_diagnostics.py`), `_local_dispatch_occupancy_evidence` (renders the denial-line fields), `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` (periodic sweep), and the `local_dispatch_denied` evidence block documented in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.
- Existing gate tests (`proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py`, helper `_make_dispatch_srv`) seed markers *and* `active=True` records for the cap-boundary cases, so switching the gate to the live count keeps their boundary semantics (they must be re-read, not assumed).

## Desired change

1. Price the prefill cap in `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` with `_get_live_prefill_in_flight_count(srv)` so a marker with no live dispatch record cannot deny a dispatch, and make the denial evidence line report that same count (gate and status cannot disagree).
2. Pop the prefill marker wherever a dispatch record is deleted — at minimum `_prune_stale_dispatch_records` and `_invalidate_session_and_slot` — so no deletion path can leave a marker behind.
3. Add a bounded reconciliation so an already-orphaned marker is dropped within one cleanup tick (the incident needed a manual `leases/release`; that must not be the only recovery).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The dispatch gate prices the prefill cap with the liveness-filtered count: a marker with no live dispatch record cannot deny a dispatch. Unit test seeds `local_prefill_in_flight` with one entry and no `local_dispatch_records`, then asserts `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` returns `(True, …)`.
2. `_prune_stale_dispatch_records` pops the pruned record's prefill marker: test asserts `local_prefill_in_flight` is empty after pruning a stale (inactive, expired) record.
3. No record-deletion path can leave an orphan marker: for every deletion helper used in production (prune, explicit release, client disconnect, request completion, watchdog, orphan sweep, session invalidation), a test asserts the marker set is a subset of the live dispatch-record session ids afterwards.
4. Regression test reproduces the incident end to end: a stale record is pruned, then a `local-preferred` request from a *different* session is admitted locally instead of returning `429 "Local admission refused"`.
5. Gate and status agree: for any state where `/llama/local/status` reports `local_prefills_in_flight=0` and `available_slots>0`, `local_dispatch_denied` cannot be emitted with `records_total=0` and `prefill_in_flight>0` (test asserts the two helpers cannot disagree, and the denial evidence line reports the gate's own count).

# Local admission over-prices a live occupant by its adaptive *lease ceiling*, refusing pinned requests that would be served in seconds

discovered-from:LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4

## Impact

Operators' locally-pinned (herdr-dispatched) requests intermittently fail with `429 Local admission refused` while the GPU is mid-prefill of another request that is about to finish — the proxy quotes a 5-minute wait for a 3-second occupant.

## Problem statement

With `X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, a request that **fits** local capacity is never promoted to a paid provider; if the local admission guard refuses it, the client gets a retryable `429 Local admission refused`. Since the orphan-marker wedge was cleared (`LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4`, 2026-11-17 16:21) the local route is healthy — 332 local streams served, zero `local_dispatch_denied ... records_total=0` — but refusals continue for a different reason:

```
18:12:56,371 local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline enforced=true
  eta_prefill_s=22.6 eta_occupancy_s=316.9 occupant_hold_s=316.9 projected_wait_s=339.5
  budget_s=30.0 deadline_s=180.0 deadline_budget_s=171.0 new_tokens=49 budget_tokens=25000
  rate_bucket=solitary busy_slots=1 in_flight_prefills=1 gate_occupancy=1 free_slot=true
  session=herdr-1794936961-3759269-19297
18:12:56,371 local_only_refused reason=prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline preference=local-preferred
  verdict=deferrable ... route=refused
```

A **49-new-token** follow-up turn was refused because the single in-flight occupant was priced at
316.9 s. That occupant was `herdr-1794938529-3818195-11862`, dispatched `18:12:54,935`, first byte
`18:12:58,613` — **3.7 s of prefill**, priced as 316.9 s (86x over).

## Root cause

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:_live_prefill_remaining_seconds` (≈3805-3897) sums, per live
prefilling record:

```
max(_occupant_prefill_remaining_seconds(record), _occupant_lease_hold_seconds(record))
```

`_occupant_lease_hold_seconds` (≈3966) returns the record's remaining `expires_at`, which is the
**adaptive dispatch-lease ceiling** from `_get_adaptive_lease_timeout_seconds` (≈1110):

```
adaptive = base_timeout(180 s) + estimated_tokens * local_dispatch_lease_per_token_seconds(0.015)
           capped at local_dispatch_lease_max_seconds(1500)
```

That ceiling is a *retention* bound chosen so a lease never lapses mid-prefill — it is ~4x the
measured prefill rate (`cold_ms_per_token=3.9`, i.e. 0.0039 s/token) plus a 180 s base. Taking
`max()` with it means the guard prices the occupant at its worst-case lease even when its
*measured* remaining service is a second or two, so `projected_wait_s` almost always exceeds
`deadline_budget_s=171 s` whenever a mid-size prompt is in flight.

The two components are known-good in opposite directions: the measured service term
(`_occupant_prefill_remaining_seconds`, `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`) re-prices from remaining *uncached*
tokens; the lease-hold term was added by `LP-0MVV29YDQ00437N6` to stop the guard *under*-pricing an
occupant that holds the slot for the whole queue budget (the 2026-10-28 `eta_occupancy_s=16.0`
under-price). The fix must keep the floor without letting the ceiling dominate measured evidence.

## Evidence (2026-11-17, live proxy `/tmp/proxy-startup-20261116T152048Z-3719311.log`)

Refusals since the wedge fix (all `preference=local-preferred`, all `verdict=deferrable`):

| time | session | new_tokens | eta_prefill_s | occupant_hold_s | projected_wait_s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17:05:11 | herdr-1794935018-… | 55 | 21.2 | 204.6 | 225.8 |
| 17:20:10 | herdr-1794935018-… | 17 | 56.4 | 401.4 | 457.8 |
| 17:36:04 | herdr-1794935018-… | 7578 | 13.9 | 413.8 | 427.7 |
| 18:02:41 | herdr-1794938529-… | 4039 | 9.8 | 327.7 | 337.5 |
| 18:12:56 | herdr-1794936961-… | 49 | 22.6 | 316.9 | 339.5 |

Every one is `free_slot=true`, `in_flight_prefills=1`, against `deadline_budget_s=171.0`.

## Scope

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: `_live_prefill_remaining_seconds`,
  `_occupant_lease_hold_seconds`, `_get_adaptive_lease_timeout_seconds` (how the hold ceiling is
  derived/decayed).
- Tests: `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `test_admission_reserve.py`,
  `test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`, `test_local_dispatch_gate.py`.

Out of scope: the `local-preferred` refusal contract (`LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY`); client-side handling of
retryable 429 (`WL-0MVSBF5XZ001H7V7`); the orphan-marker wedge (`LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4`); lease
*fairness* across renewals (`LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The occupant term no longer prices a record at its lease ceiling when measured progress says it is
   nearly done: for a record whose measured remaining prefill is `R` seconds, the term is
   `<= max(R * k, floor)` for a documented small `k` and floor (not the raw `expires_at`).
2. Regression pinned to this incident: an in-flight occupant 2 s into a 9k-token prefill (adaptive
   lease ≈317 s, `first_byte_seen=false`) must not refuse a `local-preferred` 49-new-token request
   that fits capacity and whose own prefill fits `deadline_budget_s`; the request is admitted (or
   deferred within `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) instead of 429.
3. The under-pricing cure of `LP-0MVV29YDQ00437N6` is preserved: the 2026-10-28 shape (occupant with
   no progress signal, `eta_occupancy_s` collapsing to ~0 as the queue ages) still prices the
   occupant, and its regression tests stay green.
4. Refusal diagnostics become attributable: the guard log exposes the priced components
   (measured service vs lease hold) so an over-priced refusal is provable from one log line.
5. A lease whose holder has already served its first byte, or whose record is inactive, contributes
   nothing to the occupancy term (no regression from the current filter).
6. Full suite green via the test skill.

## Notes

- No live state is stale in this failure mode: `POST /v1/leases/release` and a proxy restart do not
  help, which distinguishes it from the orphan-marker wedge. Do not "clear" it operationally.
- Retryable by contract: the refusal carries `Retry-After` / `retry_at`; the observable pain is that
  a 1-3 s wait is quoted as 5 minutes, so the client gives up or retries into the next large prefill.

## Problem statement

The first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll after a proxy restart can fire
*before* child-port discovery has succeeded, so it takes the router-port
fallback path: it logs a `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING
(`model=Qwen3`, `source=log_signal`), increments
`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
and traverses the router (`:8080`) instead of the model child port.

Consequence: every 24 h post-restart verification window on this surface
starts with a guaranteed chat-model fallback, which fails a zero-tolerance
"chat-model fallback delta == 0" acceptance criterion even when
steady-state operation is clean.

## Evidence (measured, LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window 2026-11-16T15:20:47Z → 2026-11-17T15:20:47Z)

The window is anchored to the proxy restart (`pid 3720326`, `lstart`
2026-11-16T15:20:47Z), so the process-lifetime counter delta *is* the window
delta. In `proxy.log.2026-11-16_15`, immediately after the boot sequence
(`Started TTS server`, `death capture: armed`, `Slot occupancy sampler
started (interval 10.0s)`):

```text
2026-11-16 15:20:51,411 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model child port discovered for model=Qwen3 (source=log_signal); falling back to router port 8080 — every proxy-initiated /slots poll will traverse t...
2026-11-16 15:20:51,435 - WARNING - llama-server --version returned 127
2026-11-16 15:20:51,560 - INFO - Adopted running llama-server (model=router parallel=1 router_mode=True); preserving warm prompt cache
```

- Only **one** `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker in the whole window
  (15:20:49.786, the anchor process's own boot) ⇒ no in-window restart.
- `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  = **1.0** for a process that started at the window start.
- Exactly **one** `slots_child_port_unavailable` line in the window, at
  window start **+4.4 s**; **zero** for the remaining 23 h 59 m 56 s.
- The same transient is visible in the earlier LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6 window
  (3 × `model=Qwen3`, each one within 3 s of a restart) — i.e. it is
  restart-correlated, not busy-child-correlated.

## Desired change

Make the boot-time slot poll child-port-aware: either

1. retry/defer the first slot poll until child-port discovery has resolved
   (bounded backoff), or
2. mark the poll as a boot transient so the fallback counter / WARNING are
   not incremented before discovery has had a chance to succeed.

The zero-tolerance signal (`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` + the
`slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING) must stay usable as a *regression*
signal — a boot-time increment makes a clean 24 h window indistinguishable
from one real discovery regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — After a proxy restart, the first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll
  does not increment `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and does not emit `slots_child_port_unavailable` when the model child port
  becomes discoverable within the boot window.
- **AC2** — A genuine discovery regression (child port never discoverable)
  still increments the counter and emits the WARNING; covered by a test.
- **AC3** — Reproduced by a test: boot sequence with a not-yet-ready child
  port ⇒ no fallback counter increment; child port never ready ⇒ counter
  increments once per throttled interval.
- **AC4** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the change.
- **AC5** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A restarted proxy no longer looks like it had a child-port discovery
regression on its very first slot poll, so a clean 24 h window can pass the
zero-tolerance fallback check.

# Intake Brief: Warm 99%-cached prompt priced near cold rate

## Problem statement

`prefill_eta.estimate_prefill_seconds` prices a warm, 99%-cached follow-up prompt (49 new tokens behind a 7.9 k prompt) at ~cold rate: its own-prefill ETA is **22.6 s** when measured first-byte time is **436 ms** (~0.04 ms/token). The warm prompt is refused with `429 Local admission refused` whenever any other session is prefilling, because the 22.6 s own-term pre-consumes nearly the full 30 s queue budget — even a short 22.4 s occupant causes `projected_wait=45.2 s > 30 s`.

## Users

**As** the herdr dispatch system operating locally-pinned (herdr-dispatched) panes, **I want** warm follow-up turns admitted without artificial ETA inflation, **so that** unattended dispatched panes do not die after a handful of refusals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A warm request (`cached_ratio >= 0.99`, `new_tokens <= 100`) whose bucket has sub-second measured service is priced within a documented factor of the measured service, not near cold rate: `eta_prefill_s` for the pinned 7.9 k / 49-token case is **< 5 s**. A regression test pins the 22.6 s figure as the failure mode.
2. The cached-token coefficient cannot absorb the per-request fixed overhead: pricing a prompt with `cached_ratio == 1.0` and `new_tokens == 0` stays at a documented small bound, and doubling the prompt size with identical `new_tokens` does not double its ETA.
3. Admission parity with measurement: for a bucket with >= N measured samples, the ratio `eta_prefill_s / dispatch_first_byte_ms` for warm prompts (`cached_ratio >= 0.95`) stays within the documented conservatism factor; a unit test asserts it for a seeded window.
4. A `local-preferred` request with `new_tokens <= 100` and `cached_ratio >= 0.99` is admitted (or deferred within `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) behind an occupant whose measured hold is under the queue budget, instead of refusing with `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` (regression for 18:19:10: own 22.6 s + occupant 22.4 s vs 30 s bound).
5. Conservative percentile pricing for cold prompts >= 20 k tokens (`LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN`) is unchanged: its regression tests stay green, and the cold ETA for a 25 k cold prompt is not reduced.
6. The decision log exposes the priced components (`coded_tokens`, `coded_ms_per_token`, `prefill_ms_per_token`) so an over-priced ETA is attributable from one log line.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `proxy/docs/routing.md` calibration section, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (verified via the test skill).

## Impact

A locally-pinned pane's ordinary follow-up turn (49 new tokens behind a 99 %-warm cache) is refused with `429 Local admission refused` whenever any other session is prefilling, so an unattended dispatched pane dies after a handful of turns.

## Constraints

- The fix must not degrade cold-prompt pricing (the cold-only window work of `LP-0MW957Q41002EXE2` / `LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN`).
- The `MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN = 3.0` clamp ceiling must be reconsidered: warm samples push `fitted_coded * 1.2` towards this ceiling, absorbing fixed overhead.
- The per-request fixed overhead model (`base_prefill_ms`) should be separated from the per-token cached rate in the regression.
- The percentile uplift path (`guard_cfg.eta_percentile > 0` and `prompt_tokens >= min_tokens`) must not re-introduce the problem for warm prompts at the percentile floor.
- No live state is stale in this failure mode; no restart or release is needed.

## Existing state

`prefill_eta.py` fits a two-coefficient least-squares model: `eta = coded_tokens * coded_ms + new_tokens * prefill_ms`, where `coded_tokens = est_tokens * cached_ratio` and `new_tokens = est_tokens * (1 - cached_ratio)`. The rolling window mixes cache-cold and cache-warm samples, and with warm samples dominating (coded >> new), the per-request fixed overhead is absorbed into `coded_ms_per_token` and pushed toward the `MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN = 3.0` clamp ceiling. Warm prompts are then priced at ~74 % of cold rate instead of ~1 % of cold rate.

## Desired change

Separate the per-request fixed overhead from the per-token cached rate — either by adding a `base_prefill_ms` (intercept) coefficient to the regression, or by fitting warm and cold samples separately. The warm-sample window must produce a `coded_ms_per_token` that reflects the true near-instant service time of cached tokens, bounded below by `MIN_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN = 0.05` and above by a revised ceiling. The occupancy term must continue to use the measured remaining service where available.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `_fit()`, `_fit_coefficients_from_samples()`, `coefficients()`, `estimate_prefill_seconds()`, `status_estimate()`, `MIN/MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN`, `CONSERVATISM_FACTOR`, the percentile uplift path, and the sample window selection logic
- `proxy/proxy/config.yaml` — `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens`, `MAX_CODED_MS_PER_TOKEN` (if made configurable)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta.py` — existing coefficient-fit tests
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` — conservative pricing rows (must stay green)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_cold_fit.py` — cold-sample fit tests (must stay green)
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — admission guard integration tests
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — calibration section

## Related work

| ID | Title | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MWL0LX3B004U3OR | Local admission over-prices a live occupant by its adaptive lease ceiling | Parent; different root cause (occupant pricing via lease ceiling) but same symptom (429 refusals). This item's fix is orthogonal to the parent's occupant-pricing fix. |
| LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN | Conservative prefill ETA for large prompts | Established cold-prompt percentile pricing. AC5 of this item ensures no regression. |
| LP-0MW957Q41002EXE2 | [impl] Cold-only prefill rate window and fit | Implements cold-only window for prompts >= 32 k tokens. This item targets small/warm prompts — different sample bucket, same regression framework. |
| LP-0MW957PGJ007MCDH | [test] Cold-regime calibration rows | Test items for cold-only fit. Not affected by warm-sample fix. |
| LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 | Enforce cold-prefill budget on all admission paths | Budget enforcement; not a fit-calibration item. |
| LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV | Prefill-ETA admission guard ignores occupancy | Occupancy-term fix; complementary to this item. |
| LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J | ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review | Blocked status; different scope. |
| LP-0MWKWGLRT003AUG4 | Orphan-marker wedge | Resolved; cleared the local route. |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions needed. The seed context from the auto-dispatch observation log is comprehensive: includes problem statement, root-cause hypothesis with arithmetic, evidence table, scope boundaries, and detailed acceptance criteria.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVSD3F2W006LX02** – Unit tests for new occupant-remaining pricing formula (completed)
- **LP-0MSATT20A0055YSO** – Unit tests: real cached-tokens ratio wiring (completed)
- **LP-0MVSD4O3T007CZRW** – Re-price occupant-remaining from new tokens at contended rate (completed)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — admission/queue handling and refusal path
- `proxy/README.md` — admission guard and prefill-ETA overview

## Goal

Make `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` attribute a full prefill either to an eviction (a prefix that was previously cached and then lost) or to genuinely new work, then run it over a named surviving window and commit the artifact that becomes the before/baseline measurement for this item.

## Context

The 2026-11-03 incident corpus referenced by the parent item has rotated away: `/var/log/llama-proxy/` retains daily files from 2026-11-04 (near-empty, 922 B) onward, with real content from 2026-11-07. ## Acceptance Criteria

- Attribution is measured, not assumed — over a fixed, named window a reproducible measurement (committed script or artifact) decomposes prefilled prompt tokens into (a) genuinely new tokens, where the prompt or prefix was never cached (new session or genuine divergence), and (b) re-prefills of a prefix that was previously cached and then lost, reporting the eviction-attributable share and token volume; the attribution method, its match rule and its error bounds or limitations are stated alongside the numbers.
- The match rule is explicit and conservative: an evicted entry (size in MiB, and its token count derived from the measured checkpoint term) is matched to a later full prefill only inside a bounded task-index window and a stated size tolerance; anything unmatched is classified as genuinely new work, never as eviction-attributable, and the count of unmatched candidates is reported so the conservatism is visible.
- The four token buckets (eviction-attributable, genuinely new, unattributed remainder, reused) reconcile to the reported prefilled total, and the script exits non-zero or prints an explicit warning if they do not.
- A committed artifact `docs/dev/prompt-cache-attribution-2026-11-1x.json` records the corpus file list, the window, the match rule and tolerance in `meta`, the attribution figures, and a one-line note that the 2026-11-03 window is unavailable and this is the nearest surviving substitute.

1. Extend the parser state with a bounded list of evicted entries (`size MiB`, derived token count, task index at eviction), captured from the existing `cache size limit reached, removing oldest entry` lines.
2. Classify each full prefill as attributed/genuinely new inside `_finalise`, reusing the existing `large_tokens` threshold and full-prefill detection rather than adding a parallel path.

Implementation slice for parent AC2 (a trade-off table supports the recommendation).

## Goal

Produce, from the AC1 measurement, a `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table and derive the recommended pair from it, naming the `MemAvailable` floor at which an increase must be refused — so the two knobs are decided together from one measured table instead of from a per-prompt constant inherited from the 16-prompt era.

## Context

`recommend()` currently proposes a `cache-ram` only: it reports the checkpoint term but never varies it, and it keeps `ctx-checkpoints` fixed because "fewer checkpoints can itself increase full prefills". The 2026-11-03 incident (26 retained prompts, 39,829 of 40,960 MiB) and the surviving corpora (up to 47 retained prompts) show the prompt count is the term that moved, so both knobs must appear in one table with their costs side by side. The host is 128 GiB unified memory with the documented reserve `max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)` = 12,743.7 MiB.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A trade-off table supports the recommendation — the measurement produces a `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table stating, per candidate configuration: prompts held, per-prompt state, the checkpoint term, killed prompts (prompts that would no longer fit), the checkpoint resume value (rollback granularity and the full-prefill risk of having fewer anchors), and MiB per prompt; the recommended pair is derived from that table and names the MemAvailable floor at which an increase must be refused.
- Candidates are concrete and finite: at least `ctx-checkpoints` in {32, 16, 8} x `cache-ram` in {current 40,960 MiB, the measured requirement at the observed prompt maximum, and the same capacity reached with a halved checkpoint term}, plus any value already adopted by `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51` if that item has landed.
- "Killed prompts" is defined and computed: the number of observed retained prompts that would no longer fit at that candidate, i.e. `cache_ram / per_prompt` subtracted from the measured prompt maximum, floored at zero.
- The resume value is stated qualitatively per checkpoint count (rollback granularity in tokens at the observed context, and the risk that fewer anchors means less chance of matching a reused prefix, so more full prefills), with the measured checkpoint size in MiB per checkpoint.
- The headroom verdict states which form of the invariant it uses — pre-allocation (`MemAvailable - cache-ram >= reserve`) or resident delta (only the increase must be available when the cache is already resident) — and reports both, because the two give different verdicts today; the recommended pair names the `MemAvailable` floor value in MiB that refuses a further increase.
- The table is rendered as markdown for the tuning doc and emitted in the JSON artifact, and the recommendation names the row it came from.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Refactor `recommend()` so the per-prompt and checkpoint arithmetic is a pure function of `(cache_ram, ctx_checkpoints, measured inputs)`, keeping the current single-value output backward compatible.
2. Add a `tradeoff_table(summary, ...)` builder over the finite candidate set, returning rows plus the floor verdict.
3. Add a `--tradeoff` CLI mode that prints the markdown table and includes it in `--json`; keep `--recommend` behaviour unchanged for existing reproduction commands.
4. Record the derived pair and the floor in the artifact for the same window as the AC1 measurement, then hand the values to the apply-and-pin slice.

- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-attribution-2026-11-13.json`

Verification slice for parent AC4 (post-change verification, deployed), AC5 (no throughput or latency regression), AC6 (documentation) and AC7 (full suite).

## Goal

Deploy the chosen geometry, confirm the running child carries it, and prove on a comparable window that eviction-attributable re-prefill and prefilled tokens per request fell without regressing prompt-eval throughput or client-visible first-byte latency — or record that they did not, with the reason.

## Context

Deploy is `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (detached by default, health-polled); killing the proxy is never acceptable. The restart replaces llama-server, so any request in flight at that moment fails: run it between tool calls with `/health` polled to healthy, and expect the cache to start empty, so the post-change window begins at the restart. Sessions served by the Local Proxy lose their connection only if they dispatch during the restart, which is why the deploy is its own slice rather than a step inside another change.

Baseline comparison is request-matched, not calendar-matched: the AC1 baseline artifact records the corpus file list, so the post-change window must be selected to a comparable request count and reported with `requests` alongside every per-request figure. The prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio is workload-dependent and must be reported with that caveat, never as the sole evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Post-change verification, deployed — the change is deployed with `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never by killing the proxy) and the spawned Qwen3 child is confirmed to carry the new flags; a post-change measurement over a window comparable to the AC1 baseline shows both the eviction-attributable re-prefill share and prefilled prompt tokens per request falling measurably, with the prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio recorded alongside its workload caveat.
- The spawned child's arguments are confirmed from the live process (`ps`/`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) to carry the new `--cache-ram` and `--ctx-checkpoints` values, reconciled against `models.ini`, and the confirmation is recorded with the timestamp and the child pid.
- No throughput or latency regression — prompt-eval throughput and client-visible first-byte latency measured over the same before/after windows do not regress, or any movement is attributed with evidence to a named confounder rather than to this change.
- The before/after table records per-request metrics (eviction-attributable prefills per request, prefilled tokens per request, evictions per request, first-byte median/p90, prompt-eval tokens/s) with the request count of each window, and a "Comparability" note stating how the windows were matched.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

1. Deploy with `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, poll `/health` until `status: healthy` with `llama_server_running: true`, then confirm the child's flags.
2. Run the attribution measurement over the post-change corpus once it reaches a comparable request count; commit the artifact with its `meta` block.
